data.one_liner: Mutual exclusion locks and read-write locks for asynchronous Dart code
data.what_it_does: Provides normal mutex and read-write mutex implementations to protect critical sections of code and prevent race conditions when using asynchronous operations. Includes convenience methods like protect, protectRead, and protectWrite to safely acquire and release locks.
use_when: You have asynchronous operations inside critical sections that risk race conditions
You need multiple read locks to exist simultaneously while restricting write locks to a single exclusive instance
avoid_when: Your critical section only contains synchronous code, which cannot be interrupted in Dart
Your critical section does not involve shared data or resources accessible by other asynchronous code
strengths: Supports both normal mutexes and read-write mutexes
Convenience methods ensure locks are always released correctly via try-finally blocks
weaknesses: Requires proper management to avoid deadlocks in complex asynchronous flows
